comparisons.peer_topic: CET1 and leverage ratio regulatory minimums
comparisons.peer_summary: The CET1 capital regulatory minimum includes the Corporation's G-SIB surcharge and statutory capital buffer (SCB), while the SLR regulatory minimum includes a 2.0 percent leverage buffer; countercyclical capital buffers were zero for both periods.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC disclose the composition of their CET1 capital regulatory minimums, which include a base minimum, a G-SIB surcharge, and a Stress Capital Buffer (SCB). However, the specific buffer values differ between the two firms for the same period. GS reports an SCB of 3.2% (noted in summary as 6.2% for Standardized, but the peer text clarifies the breakdown) and a G-SIB surcharge of 3.0%, whereas BAC reports an SCB of 3.2% and a G-SIB surcharge of 3.0% for December 31, 2024. Wait, looking closely at GS text: 'SCB of 6.2% as of December 2024... under the Standardized'. Looking at BAC text: 'SCB... of 3.2 percent at December 31, 2024'. There is a discrepancy in the reported SCB values between the two disclosures for the same date, which is a meaningful difference in regulatory capital requirements. Both confirm a 3.0% G-SIB surcharge and 0% countercyclical buffer.

sentences.text: • As of both December 2024 and December 2023, under both the Standardized and Advanced Capital Rules, the CET1 capital ratio requirement includes a minimum of 4.5%, the Tier 1 capital ratio requirement includes a minimum of 6.0% and the Total capital ratio requirement includes a minimum of 8.0%. These requirements also include the capital conservation buffer requirements, consisting of the G-SIB surcharge (Method 2) of 3.0% and the countercyclical capital buffer, which the FRB has set to zero percent. In addition, the capital conservation buffer requirements include the stress capital buffer (SCB) of 6.2% as of December 2024 and 5.5% as of December 2023 under the Standardized Capital Rules and a buffer of 2.5% as of both December 2024 and December 2023 under the Advanced Capital Rules.

(2)The CET1 capital regulatory minimum is the sum of the CET1 capital ratio minimum of 4.5 percent, the Corporation's G-SIB surcharge of 3.0 percent at December 31, 2024 and 2.5 percent at December 31, 2023, and SCB (under the Standardized approach) of 3.2 percent at December 31, 2024 and 2.5 percent at December 31, 2023.
The countercyclical capital buffer was zero for both periods.

comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPM disclose the specific components of their regulatory capital ratio requirements, including the G-SIB surcharge and the Stress Capital Buffer (SCB). A key difference is the G-SIB surcharge rate: GS applies a 3.0% surcharge (Method 2), while JPM applies a higher 4.5% surcharge (Method 2). Similarly, their SCBs differ: GS reports a 6.2% SCB under Standardized rules, whereas JPM reports a 3.3% SCB under its Standardized ratios. Both firms report a 0% countercyclical buffer.

sentences.text: • As of both December 2024 and December 2023, under both the Standardized and Advanced Capital Rules, the CET1 capital ratio requirement includes a minimum of 4.5%, the Tier 1 capital ratio requirement includes a minimum of 6.0% and the Total capital ratio requirement includes a minimum of 8.0%. These requirements also include the capital conservation buffer requirements, consisting of the G-SIB surcharge (Method 2) of 3.0% and the countercyclical capital buffer, which the FRB has set to zero percent. In addition, the capital conservation buffer requirements include the stress capital buffer (SCB) of 6.2% as of December 2024 and 5.5% as of December 2023 under the Standardized Capital Rules and a buffer of 2.5% as of both December 2024 and December 2023 under the Advanced Capital Rules.

The CET1, Tier 1 and Total capital ratio requirements each include a respective minimum requirement plus a GSIB surcharge of 4.5% as calculated under Method 2; plus a 3.3% SCB for Basel III Standardized ratios and a fixed 2.5% capital conservation buffer for Basel III Advanced ratios.
The countercyclical buffer is currently set to 0% by the federal banking agencies.

comparisons.peer_topic: Capital Buffer Requirement Definition and Composition
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm's capital buffer requirement represents the CET1 capital needed above minimum risk-based requirements to avoid restrictions on capital distributions and discretionary bonuses. Under the Standardized Approach, this requirement is the sum of the SCB, G-SIB surcharge, and CCyB, while under the Advanced Approach, it includes the 2.5% conservation buffer, G-SIB surcharge, and CCyB.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and MS define and disclose the composition of their capital buffer requirements that sit atop minimum regulatory capital ratios. Both firms distinguish between the Standardized and Advanced approaches. For the Advanced Approach, both GS and MS specify a 2.5% capital conservation buffer component within their buffer requirements. MS explicitly defines the buffer as the amount needed to avoid restrictions on distributions, composed of the SCB, G-SIB surcharge, and CCyB under the Standardized approach, similar to the components GS lists in its conservation buffer description.

sentences.text: • As of both December 2024 and December 2023, under both the Standardized and Advanced Capital Rules, the CET1 capital ratio requirement includes a minimum of 4.5%, the Tier 1 capital ratio requirement includes a minimum of 6.0% and the Total capital ratio requirement includes a minimum of 8.0%. These requirements also include the capital conservation buffer requirements, consisting of the G-SIB surcharge (Method 2) of 3.0% and the countercyclical capital buffer, which the FRB has set to zero percent. In addition, the capital conservation buffer requirements include the stress capital buffer (SCB) of 6.2% as of December 2024 and 5.5% as of December 2023 under the Standardized Capital Rules and a buffer of 2.5% as of both December 2024 and December 2023 under the Advanced Capital Rules.

The capital buffer requirement represents the amount of CET1 capital the Firm must maintain above the minimum risk-based capital requirements in order to avoid restrictions on the Firm's ability to make capital distributions, including the payment of dividends and the repurchase of stock, and to pay discretionary bonuses to executive officers.

The Firm's capital buffer requirement computed under the standardized approaches for calculating credit risk and market risk RWA ("Standardized Approach") is equal to the sum of the SCB, G-SIB capital surcharge and CCyB, and the capital buffer requirement computed under the applicable advanced approaches for calculating credit risk, market risk and operational risk RWA ("Advanced Approach") is equal to the sum of the 2.5% capital conservation buffer, G-SIB capital surcharge and CCyB.
